title: Neutron Stars
objective: After this level you can describe neutron stars and how dense they are.
summary: A supernova can leave a neutron star: about 20 km across, heavier than the Sun, so dense a teaspoon weighs billions of tons.

cards.headline: A star heavier than the Sun, squeezed into the size of a city.
cards.body: Take more mass than the Sun and squeeze it into a ball the size of a city. That’s not a thought experiment. It’s what a massive star leaves behind when it explodes.

cards.headline: What a supernova leaves behind
cards.body: When a massive star explodes as a supernova, not everything flies away. Its core collapses into a neutron star: a ball only about 20 km across, about the size of a city, yet it can hold more mass than the Sun. That’s more than a whole Sun’s worth of stuff in a space you could bike across in about an hour. The explosion is the loud part. The leftover is the strange part.
cards.callout: ~20 km across, more mass than the Sun

cards.headline: Crushed to neutrons
cards.body: How do you fit a sun into a city? Gravity crushes the collapsing core so hard that its matter becomes mostly neutrons, packed tightly together. Remember Level 68’s white dwarf, where a teaspoon weighed several tons? A teaspoon of neutron star would weigh billions of tons on Earth. Your sugar spoon has never worked so hard. And many neutron stars spin many times per second, with magnetic fields far stronger than Earth’s. Hold on to that spin.

cards.headline: Neutron stars: understood
learned: A neutron star is a supernova’s collapsed core
It can hold more mass than the Sun
A teaspoon would weigh billions of tons

questions.prompt: About how wide is a neutron star?

options.label: About the size of the Sun
About 20 km, the size of a city

questions.explanation: A neutron star packs more than the Sun’s mass into a ball only about 20 km across.

questions.prompt: What makes a neutron star so incredibly dense?

options.label: Gravity crushes its matter into tightly packed neutrons
It is made of solid iron
It absorbs nearby planets
options.rationale: Density comes from collapse, not eating planets.

questions.explanation: The collapsing core is crushed until its matter is mostly neutrons packed tightly together.

questions.prompt: From Level 68: a white dwarf teaspoon weighs several tons. How does a neutron star compare?

options.label: It is lighter than a white dwarf
It is about the same weight
options.rationale: It’s billions of tons per teaspoon.

options.label: It weighs nothing, being a star
A teaspoon weighs billions of tons

questions.explanation: A white dwarf teaspoon weighs a few tons; a neutron star teaspoon weighs billions of tons.
